name: Knight against bishop — the structure decides

plans.label: Open a file and keep pawns on both wings
plans.description: Open the pawn structure and create play on both wings: at least one file is fully open and White still has pawns on both the queenside and the kingside.

success.note: RESTATED PLAN. The plan was 'Open the position, play both wings', whose success was two structural judgments. It is now the two facts underneath them: some file is fully open, and White has pawns on both wings. 'Open' here means a pawnless file, which is stricter than the word means at the board. Original success note: 'Open-versus-fixed and one-wing-versus-two are structural judgments the shipped features cannot express.'

plans.label: The far passer outruns the knight
plans.description: A passed pawn on the rook's file is the bishop's favourite: the bishop escorts or stops it from across the board while the knight's short legs and the edge's missing squares make its geometry ugly.

success.note: A rook-file passer is the shape; the knight's actual travel distance is geometry the signature cannot count.

plans.label: Keep every pawn on one side of the board
plans.description: Keep all play on one wing; a one-front board is the knight's board, because reach beats range when nothing is far away. The fixing half of the old plan is not measured here.

success.note: RESTATED PLAN. The plan was 'Fix the pawns, keep one front', two claims of which only one is expressible. It is now the one front alone: every pawn left on the board, of either colour, stands on one side of the d/e boundary. Fixedness is dropped, not measured. Original success note: 'Holding-by-structure is an outcome; fixedness is not in the feature set.' Degenerate-case guard: the earlier draft of this signature was vacuously true over an empty piece set, so an existence clause was added. A pawnless board satisfied 'every pawn is on one side' with no pawns at all; at least one pawn must now exist.

plans.label: Anchor the knight on a hole
plans.description: Plant the knight on a protected square the bishop cannot contest — a hole of the wrong colour for the bishop — and make it the fixed point the defence turns on; an anchored knight blockades, forks, and never gets traded at a bad moment.

success.note: A Black knight standing on a square that Tabiya's strict outpost detector calls an outpost: pawn-defended, on relative ranks four to six, and safe from any pawn eviction. The earlier note declined this because naming one square would bind family prose to one position; enumerating the whole domain — the eighteen non-edge squares where a Black outpost can exist — does not. It says the knight is anchored; it does not say the bishop cannot contest the square.

watch: The trigger sees only the material census — bishop for White, knight for Black; whether the structure favours knight or bishop (fixed or fluid, one wing or two) is exactly the judgment it cannot make.
Pawn counts are not expressible; this fires level or unbalanced alike. Count the pawns.
Colour convention: White is authored as the bishop side. Mirror the plans when the knight side is yours; the trigger fires only for this orientation.
typicalMistakes: Letting the pawns fix on your bishop's colour, converting the bishop side's edge into a bad-bishop ending.
Opening a second front while holding the knight — the knight cannot defend two wings.
Trading bishop for knight, or knight for bishop, into an uncounted pawn ending; the minor-piece battle is worthless the move after it is resolved.
Evicting the anchored knight with a pawn move that leaves a worse hole behind.

sources: Family per design/04-content-architecture.md section 4 (minor piece: knight vs bishop by structure).
Tablebase honesty: typical positions of this family exceed seven pieces; no tablebase ground truth exists for them and none was consulted.
UNGROUNDED: plan, watch, and mistake prose is authored endgame-literature consensus rendered by the author; no engine or tablebase has graded any claim in this entry.
Trigger gap: every structural claim that decides this family — fixedness, wing count, colour complexes, knight anchors — is outside the shipped vocabulary; the trigger names the census only.
